title: The Malevolent 3
content:
He took barely a single step back before his ankle rolled, sending him stumbling forward as if he were about to hit the dirt on his knees.

Lan Wangji’s composure shattered. Lunging forward in a blur, he locked an iron grip onto Wei Wuxian’s wrist—just as he had on Dafan Mountain—steadying him before dropping to one knee to examine his leg.

Thoroughly startled, Wei Wuxian waved his free hand frantically. "Wait, wait, wait, Hanguang-jun! There's really no need for this!"

Lan Wangji tilted his chin up, pinning him with those pale, glassy eyes, before looking right back down to shove the fabric of his trousers up. Hand held fast in that unbreakable grip, Wei Wuxian could only look to the heavens in defeat.

The skin of his leg was a solid, bruised mottled black—eaten alive by the Malignant Curse Mark.

Lan Wangji stared at the rotting mark for a long time, his voice coming out tight and raspy. "...I was gone for only a few hours."

Wei Wuxian gave a helpless shrug. "A few hours is an eternity. Anything can happen in that time. Come on, up you get, Your Majesty."

Hooking a hand under Lan Wangji's arm, he hauled him back to his feet. "It's just a garden-variety curse mark. When the thing comes knocking, I'll just beat it to a pulp. You'll help me out, right, Hanguang-jun? I can't handle it on my own. Did you catch the guy? Was it him? Where is he?"

Lan Wangji’s gaze drifted toward a hanging shop banner fluttering in the distance down the quiet avenue.

"Let's get this stone fortress mess sorted out first," Wei Wuxian said, turning toward the banner. He hadn't noticed earlier, but his legs felt leaden and prickly—leftover static from Zidian's lash. At least Jiang Cheng still had the sense to throttle the whip's voltage; otherwise, he'd be walking around as a lightning-charred corpse.

Behind him, Lan Wangji spoke.

"Wei Ying."

Wei Wuxian’s stride hitched for the barest fraction of a second. Turning back with complete nonchalance, as though the name had washed right over him, he asked, "Yeah? What's up?"

"Did you take it from Jin Ling?"

It wasn't a question; it was a flat statement of fact.

Wei Wuxian offered neither confirmation nor denial.

"You ran into Jiang Wanyin," Lan Wangji added.

Given the telltale burn marks left by Zidian overlapping the dark rot, it wasn't a hard deduction to make. Wei Wuxian faced him properly. "As long as two people are breathing the same air, they're bound to bump into each other eventually."

"Stop walking," Lan Wangji said.

Wei Wuxian smirked. "What, if I don't walk, are you going to carry me on your back?"

Lan Wangji stared back in deadpan silence.

The smirk froze on Wei Wuxian's face, a sudden prickle of dread creeping up his spine.

The Lan Zhan of the past would have choked on his own righteous fury, thrown him a death glare, and stormed off, or simply frozen him out. But this new, upgraded model? There was no telling what he'd pull.

Sure enough, Lan Wangji stepped right into his space, angling his shoulders and bending his knees, genuinely looking like he was about to lower his noble, untouchable self to offer him a piggyback.

Wei Wuxian nearly jumped out of his skin. "Hold on, hold on! I was messing around! Zidian just shocked my legs numb, that's all—it's not like the bones are snapped. A grown man getting piggybacked down a public street? It looks ridiculous!"

Lan Wangji asked, "Does it?"

Wei Wuxian retorted, "Does it look dignified to you?!"

After a beat of heavy silence, Lan Wangji murmued, "You carried me on your back once."

Wei Wuxian blinked. "Did I? Why don't I remember that?"

Lan Wangji’s voice was as cool as fresh snow. "You never remember these things."

"Everyone says my memory's garbage," Wei Wuxian muttered, rubbing his nose. "Fine, so it's bad. Either way, no piggybacks."

"Are you certain?"

Wei Wuxian crossed his arms with absolute conviction. "Dead certain."

They stood locked in a stubborn standoff under the moonlight.

Without warning, Lan Wangji hooked an arm around Wei Wuxian's back, dipped low, and swept his other arm clean under the crook of his knees.

Wei Wuxian was shorter in this body, and significantly lighter. In one fluid swoop, his boots left the ground, scooped up and cradled securely against Lan Wangji’s chest in a bridal carry.

Wei Wuxian had braced for every possible outcome of refusing a piggyback, but this had never once crossed his mind. Across two lifetimes, he had never been manhandled like this.

He let out a strangled, horrified yelp: "Lan Zhan!!!"

Lan Wangji cradled him without so much as a tremor in his stride, his reply infuriatingly steady: "You said no piggyback."

Wei Wuxian choked, "That didn't mean you could carry me like a maiden!"

Fortunately, midnight had claimed the town, leaving the streets blissfully deserted; at least he wouldn't be publicly humiliated. Besides, Wei Wuxian had never been cursed with a thin skin. After a few paces, he relaxed into the hold, reaching up to toy with the silk ribbon trailing down Lan Wangji’s chest, giving it a playful tug.

"Trying to see who can be more shameless, are we?" he grinned.

That cool, crisp scent of sandalwood enveloped him. Lan Wangji didn't spare him a glance, staring dead ahead, an unshakeable pillar of virtue and stoic grace. Seeing the man play deaf and dumb, Wei Wuxian twirled the ribbon between his fingers, musing inwardly: Who knew Lan Zhan could hold a grudge like this? Every little prank I pulled on him back in the day, he's paying back in full, tit for tat, just to watch me squirm. Talk about personal growth. His cultivation isn't the only thing that's leveled up—his skin has gotten thicker, too.

"Lan Zhan," Wei Wuxian murmured, "did you figure out who I was all the way back on Dafan Mountain?"

"Mn."

Wei Wuxian arched a brow. "How?"

Lan Wangji’s lashes fluttered downward, casting a brief, heavy look at him. "You want to know?"

"Yeah," Wei Wuxian said, leaning in.

"You told me yourself."

Wei Wuxian frowned. "I told you? Was it because of Jin Ling? Because I summoned Wen Ning? Neither of those makes sense."

A faint ripple seemed to stir behind those pale amber irises—a quiet, fleeting current that dissolved back into an untroubled pool before it could be caught.

His tone hardened into an austere mask: "Think for yourself."

"I'm only asking because I can't figure it out!"

No matter how much he poked and prodded after that, Lan Wangji kept his mouth shut.

Cradling Wei Wuxian against his chest, he kicked through the front doors of the inn. Aside from the clerk behind the counter spraying tea all over the ledger, nobody else was awake to make a scene.

Reaching the upper floor, they stopped outside a private chamber.

"All right, we're here," Wei Wuxian said, tapping his shoulder. "Put me down. You need a free hand to open the—"

Before the word could leave his mouth, Lan Wangji committed a blatant breach of etiquette. It was likely the very first coarse, unrefined motion he had ever executed in his entire pristine life.

Still carrying Wei Wuxian in his arms, he reared back and booted the door off its latch.

Bam!

The double doors flew inward, revealing a man shrinking awkwardly in the center of the room. The captive immediately burst into tears: "Hanguang-jun, I don't know, I swear I don't know anything, I—"

Catching sight of the posture in which the two men had breached the threshold, the man's jaw dropped, his gaze turning utterly glassy as he stammered out the finish: "...I really don't know anything."

True to his moniker: Three-Times-Ignorant.

Lan Wangji ignored the spectacle completely, carrying Wei Wuxian across the threshold before gently setting him down onto a woven rush mat. Looking visibly traumatized, Nie Huaisang snapped his folding fan open, clamping it over his face to shield his eyes.

Wei Wuxian peeked over the top of the fan, taking a good look at his former desk-mate. All these years down the line, the man hadn't aged a day. He looked exactly as he had in their youth: blessed with the delicate, cultured features of a poet, yet saddled with the spineless, moldable demeanor of soft dough. His robes were tailored from exquisite, tasteful silks—impeccably styled with effortless flair, clearly the product of painstaking daily grooming. Calling him the leader of a prominent sect felt like an insult to the title; he looked far more like an idle, wealthy fop who spent his life floating down pleasure barges. Put him in dragon robes and he still wouldn't look like an emperor; strap a heavy sabre to his hip and he’d never resemble a warrior.

Faced with stubborn, trembling silence, Lan Wangji reached into his sleeve and dropped the torn scrap of fabric the hound had bitten off onto the tabletop.

Nie Huaisang clutched his shredded sleeve, his face a storm of misery. "I was just out for a stroll. I really don't know anything."

Wei Wuxian chimed in, "Since you don't know, how about I walk you through it? Maybe your memory will clear up along the way."

Nie Huaisang fidgeted behind his fan, trapped and stammering.

Wei Wuxian laid it out: "The rumors of a 'Man-Eating Ridge' and a 'Man-Eating Castle' have been circulating around Qinghe for ages, yet there isn't a single recorded victim to back the tales up. That makes it a deliberate hoax. A terrifying ghost story keeps ordinary mortals far away from Xinglu Ridge, which means the rumor was meant to serve as a defensive perimeter. The first line of defense."

"Where there's a first line, there's a second. The walking corpses patrolling the trails form your second barrier. Even if a fearless traveler ignores the campfire tales and climbs the ridge, coming face-to-face with shambling dead men will send them sprinting back down the mountain. But those corpses are sluggish and harmless, ensuring no innocent blood is actually spilled."

"The third line is that illusionary maze encircling the stone fortresses. The first two traps are meant for commoners; this one is built specifically to turn away wandering cultivators. Still, it only stops the average novice. The moment someone shows up with a high-grade compass, an elite spiritual hound, or the raw power of someone like Hanguang-jun, the maze gets cracked wide open."

"Three layers of security, all designed to keep that stone fortress buried in the woods. As for who built it? That's obvious. This is Qinghe Nie territory; nobody else has the authority or the resources to construct a three-tiered perimeter in your backyard without raising hell. Not to mention, you happened to be lurking outside the breach yourself, leaving hard evidence in a dog's jaws."

"Why did the Qinghe Nie Clan build a man-eating castle on Xinglu Ridge? Where did all the skeletons packed inside the walls come from? Did the stones really eat them? Sect Leader Nie, if you don't spill the truth right here, the moment this leaks to the other clans, you'll be facing a joint interrogation. And when that day comes, nobody is going to listen to your excuses—and nobody is going to believe a word you say."

Nie Huaisang slumped, completely defeated. "...It's not a man-eating castle. That... that's just my family's ancestral tomb!"

Wei Wuxian raised an eyebrow. "An ancestral tomb? What kind of family buries unsheathed sabres instead of coffined corpses?"

Looking like he was about to weep, Nie Huaisang pleaded, "Hanguang-jun, before I open my mouth, can you swear an oath? For the sake of our clans' long-standing friendship, and because my late brother was sworn brothers with your elder brother... Whatever I say next, neither you nor the gentleman beside you can breathe a single word of it to the outside world. If the truth ever blows wide open, I need you two to stand as witnesses and speak on my behalf. You've always been a man of your word; if you swear it, I'll talk."

Lan Wangji inclined his head. "As you wish."

Wei Wuxian leaned forward. "You claim it isn't a man-eating castle, so it's never devoured anyone?"

Nie Huaisang gritted his teeth, confessing with a squeak: "...It has."

Wei Wuxian whistled. "Wow."

"Just once!" Nie Huaisang scrambled to add, waving his hands frantically. "And it wasn't even entirely our fault! That happened decades ago! The whole 'Man-Eating Castle' rumor started back then—I... I just fanned the flames a little and blew the gossip out of proportion to keep people away!"
